plaintext.source: A pencil decipherment of the time at the head of the form, "Total 160 h - Diga si viene refuerzo y", then a faint last word under the CEHM watermark that the PR #831 review could not read: 9 of the 10 coded words. Not in the typed list CMXV.18.1795.1 (searched by the contributor).

transcription.source: Daniel Jalkut with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), from the CEHM viewer image (study copy, not redistributed); PR #831, the block CMXV.15.1430.3-3 of the siblings file
transcription.notes: Telegram of 4:37 pm; all 10 groups are coded: 49 letters, measured with _check_profile.py --measure --letters on the two lines of its block; '|' marks the pencil strokes of the decipherer of the time. The PR #831 review compared all 10 groups and the pencil line with the CEHM image (a model's comparison).

system.summary: Five pairs of letters swap in place in both directions (L-A, N-E, R-I, S-O, T-U); every other letter is unchanged; four words of a Spanish telegram are coded.

prior_solution.where: The key card for the recipient (CMXV.16.1557.1, scan 16) in the same fonds gives the pairs. For CMXV.15.1420.3-6 no decipherment stands on the sheet and the contributor found none in print. CMXV.15.1430.3-3 carries a pencil decipherment of the time at the head of the form (9 of its 10 words), which Daniel Jalkut found when he checked his decode against the sheet (PR #831); it is not in the typed list CMXV.18.1795.1.

conditions.human_role: William Echols submitted the transcription, the key and the reading of CMXV.15.1420.3-6 (issue #351), made with GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex; the project re-ran the four decryptions and has not compared that telegram with its image. Daniel Jalkut (PR #831, with Claude Code) transcribed CMXV.15.1430.3-3 from the CEHM image, applied the card and found the pencil decipherment on the form. The PR #831 review (an AI agent) compared the card with scan 16 and the 1430.3-3 groups and gloss with the image; no person has.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) in Claude Code, run by Daniel Jalkut (CMXV.15.1430.3-3, PR #831)

solution.what: The contributor transcribed the two CEHM images; the project did not see them.
The contributor applied the five letter pairs of the Hernández key card (CMXV.16.1557.1, scan 16) to the four coded words: all four give Spanish words (VILLARREAL, SALDRA, LLEVANDO, CANON).
Project check: the four coded words decrypted again with the five pairs agree with the contributor's decryption on all 29 letters (VERIFICATION.md). No scan or card compared.
Daniel Jalkut (PR #831) transcribed CMXV.15.1430.3-3 from the CEHM image, with nine other sibling telegrams of catalogue 1462 (files in ../duron1911/siblings/).

Hypothesis that the Presidio telegrams of 27-31 March 1911 signed B. Hernández, B. H. Leroy or E. H. Leroy use the Hernández card, as 1420.3-6 does. Applied to 1430.3-3 it gives 'total cieto sesenta hombres digas iviene reouerzo y canon': two slips, the n of ciento missing and s (plain o) where refuerzo wants f.

Contributor's control: the decode agrees with the pencil decipherment of the time at the head of the form ('Total 160 h - Diga si viene refuerzo y'), which was not used to find the key; the gloss gives ciento (160) and refuerzo, the two words with a slip.

PR #831 review (an AI agent, two rounds): own decoder from key.tsv equal to the filed decryption of 1430.3-3 (49 letters); all 10 groups and the pencil line compared with the CEHM image; the card compared with CMXV.16.1557.1 scan 16, typed 'Hernández : l n r s t / a e i o u', the five pairs of key.tsv.

Integration of PR #831: CMXV.15.1430.3-3 filed here (one key, one entry); its files stay in ../duron1911/siblings/ and are referenced; own decode from key.tsv repeated, equal to the filed decryption. The four other Hernández-card telegrams of PR #831 (1420.5-6, 10 sure words of 19; 1420.6-6, 1432.3-4 and 1447.1-3, decoded, not read) are not filed here: they would make this target read in part, and that is the owner's decision.

validation.notes: Four coded words are too few for a language-model test, and the key is the archive's card, not a recovered key.

outcome.method_basis: The key is the archive's own card for the recipient, found in the same fonds by the contributor and applied; the project re-ran the four decryptions. The key was not recovered from the ciphertext. CMXV.15.1430.3-3 (part 2) is read from the pencil decipherment of the time on its form, which the card confirms and completes (the last word, cañón).

texts.label: Telegram of 27 March 1911 to Braulio Hernández (CEHM-Carso CMXV.15.1420.3-6)
texts.summary: A telegram from Federico González Garza at El Paso to Braulio Hernández at Presidio: did you receive the pills? you should stay there; Villarreal will leave Wednesday or Thursday, taking a cannon; write back.

reading_review.note: Read the telegram as Spanish sentences: the four decoded words fill the gaps of the clear text and make coherent clauses; the transcription is the contributor's and was not compared with the scan.

texts.label: Telegram of 28 March 1911, "E H Leroy" (Braulio Hernández) to Federico González Garza (CEHM-Carso CMXV.15.1430.3-3)
texts.summary: Braulio Hernández ("E H Leroy") at Presidio to González Garza at El Paso: a total of one hundred and sixty men; say whether reinforcements and the cannon are coming. Deciphered at the time in pencil on the form; the Hernández card gives the same text.
texts.note: The siblings files of PR #831 hold ten telegrams: this entry is the block or section headed CMXV.15.1430.3-3 in each, and its English is in the same section of reading.md. Read from the decipherment of the time: ciento (160) and refuerzo stand in the pencil gloss, so all 10 cipher words are read. The reading marks cie{n}to and re{f}uerzo because the card's output has a slip in each; the card alone gives 8 of 10 (2 holes, which the short-text floor would also allow).

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #831 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Two clauses read as Spanish against the translation: 'Total ciento sesenta hombres. Diga si viene refuerzo y cañón.' Checked: own decode from key.tsv equal to the filed decryption (49 letters); the PR #831 review compared all 10 groups and the pencil line 'Total 160 h - Diga si viene refuerzo y' with the CEHM image, and the crop of that line was looked at again here; 8 words come from the card alone, ciento and refuerzo carry a slip each and stand in the gloss, and the last word, cañón, comes from the card (CLESE, as in 1420.3-6). Not checked: the faint last word of the gloss, under the watermark; the form's other lines. A model's reading: no person has checked it.
